touches.text: A ticket's plan is a plan: constraints, tasks, dependencies, resources. Q#100 answered 2026-11-14 (open-91e33982f3d5, open-7c607df497bd): "when I use microsoft project to make a plan, it has constraints, tasks, dependencies, and resources. that's a plan. a list of decisions does not look like a plan to me." Then: "we will go with this as you've described it for now ... lets go with it as you say and see how it works. i would also say that the shift from decisions to plan steps means that the first decision (on conversion) will shape some of the plan, and later steps may reshape some of those. we should check for coherence at the end. any plan that's too big probably needs to be multiple tickets. real dependencies are things like we can't test the bus envelope shape until the bus works. and will shape ticket order more than anything else. resources are preexisting machines/tools/even design patterns if we need to state them explicitly." -amm Then, same day (open-7aee6f89e4d9, open-82f27105184f): "we can specify a task order, but again it should be based on dependencies. or maybe... rather than tasks should we be focused on outcomes?" / "yes indeed i think that's the thing." / "an outcome can hide the how, and i try and specify the how when i'm attached to it, like encapsulation, or the bus being the only communication channel or whichever. yes, we're in agreement. signed -amm" -amm

The reading: - A plan is three parts. Constraints: the bounds, plus every how Akien is attached to, carried verbatim (encapsulation, the bus as the only channel, ...): a how he states is a constraint. Then outcomes. Then resources. - An outcome is {n, claim, writes_to, reads, after: [n or a ticket id], via?}. The claim is falsifiable, one proof tooth per outcome. The falsifier's clauses merge into the outcomes; there is no separate falsifier list. Old clause n stays outcome n; outcomes made from decisions number after them. via (optional) names the tool or pattern to use, drawn from resources. - Order comes from after: only real dependencies ("can't test the bus envelope shape until the bus works"), which also shape ticket order. Nothing invents them; list order is reading order only. - Resources: pre-existing machines, tools and design patterns, named when they need stating. - The migration is two steps. Mechanical, on every open ticket now: the plan moves to the new field with clause numbers kept, the trail moves whole to the log, by moves to the log. Judgement, when a ticket is next opened for build, never in bulk: each decision becomes an outcome or a constraint, then a coherence check (every step reads as current; a conflict moves to the log or is named). - CC inference: the mechanical step writes each old decision as an outcome numbered after the clauses, carrying its text and no claim; an outcome with no claim is awaiting judgement and holds BUILDME until the judgement step gives it a claim or moves it to constraints. - akienasus_cc_0 - During the change every reader accepts both shapes. Readers are censused first; one sibling ticket per reader component (RULE 1). - The cast door refuses an outcome with no falsifiable claim, and a plan of more than about 7 outcomes, naming children; each refusal is recorded so the ceiling can be tuned (the 7 is CC's guess). - The [?] markers go. - Tickets: aa3e9a70db47 is the migration (rehearsal); d421051bc1f7 is the hand-built worked example; each reader component has its sibling. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator -amm

Skills (skills/: cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...) are Claude Code's. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. WHY: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster; a first charting pass done in deterministic Python with no LLM until after saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
